title: Patty Hearst
wiki_lead:
Patricia Campbell Hearst (born February 20, 1954) is an American actress and member of the Hearst family. She is the granddaughter of newspaper publisher and politician William Randolph Hearst.
Hearst first became known for the events following her 1974 kidnapping by the Symbionese Liberation Army (SLA). She was found and arrested 19 months after being abducted, by which time she was a fugitive wanted for serious crimes committed with members of the group. She was held in custody, and there was speculation before trial that her family's resources would enable her to avoid time in prison.
At her trial, the prosecution suggested that Hearst had joined the Symbionese Liberation Army of her own volition. However, she testified that she had been raped and threatened with death while held captive. In 1976, she was convicted for the crime of bank robbery and sentenced to 35 years in prison, later reduced to seven years. Her sentence was commuted by President Jimmy Carter, and she was later pardoned by President Bill Clinton.
In the 1990s, she began acting in films and television after being approached by film director John Waters.

Early life
Patricia Campbell Hearst was born on February 20, 1954, in San Francisco, California, the third of five daughters of Randolph Apperson Hearst and Catherine Wood Campbell. She was raised primarily in Hillsborough and attended the private Crystal Springs School for Girls there, Sacred Heart in Atherton, and the Santa Catalina School in Monterey. She attended Menlo College in Atherton, California before transferring to the University of California, Berkeley.
Hearst's grandfather William Randolph Hearst created the multinational mass media and business information conglomerate Hearst Communications. Her great-grandmother was philanthropist Phoebe Hearst. The family wielded immense political influence and had opposed organized labor, gold mine workers' interests, and communism since before World War II. Hearst's father was among a number of heirs to the family fortune and did not control the Hearst interests. Her parents had not considered it necessary to take preventive measures to ensure their children's personal security. At the time of her abduction, Hearst was a sophomore at Berkeley studying art history. She lived with her fiancé Steven Weed in an apartment in Berkeley.


Symbionese Liberation Army (SLA)


Kidnapping
On February 4, 1974, 19-year-old Hearst was kidnapped from her Berkeley apartment. A small urban guerrilla left-wing group called the Symbionese Liberation Army (SLA) claimed responsibility for the abduction and demanded the release of recently arrested SLA members Joe Remiro and Russ Little.
After the state refused to free the men, the SLA demanded that Hearst's family distribute $70 worth of food to every needy Californian, an operation that would cost an estimated $400 million. In response, Hearst's father obtained a loan and arranged the immediate donation of $2 million worth of food to the poor
grok_lead: Patricia Campbell Hearst (born February 20, 1954), commonly known as Patty Hearst, is an American heiress and granddaughter of newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst who gained notoriety after her abduction by the Symbionese Liberation Army, a radical left-wing group espousing revolutionary violence against perceived capitalist oppression. On February 4, 1974, the 19-year-old Hearst was kidnapped at gunpoint from her Berkeley, California apartment by SLA members, who held her captive for 57 days under conditions she later described as involving isolation, threats, and coercion. Surveillance video from the April 15, 1974 armed robbery of a Hibernia Bank branch in San Francisco captured Hearst, masked and wielding an M1 carbine rifle, actively participating alongside SLA comrades by shouting commands at customers and tellers to remain still while over $10,000 was stolen. After 19 months as a fugitive, during which she issued statements adopting the SLA alias "Tania" and denouncing her family and the U.S. government, Hearst was arrested in San Francisco on September 18, 1975. Her 1976 federal trial centered on defenses of duress and psychological coercion akin to brainwashing, but the jury convicted her of bank robbery and use of a firearm in a felony, leading to a seven-year sentence; she served 22 months before President Jimmy Carter commuted it in 1979, followed by a full pardon from President Bill Clinton on January 20, 2001. Post-release, Hearst married her bodyguard Bernard Shaw in 1979, with whom she had two daughters, Gillian and Lydia; she co-authored a memoir recounting her experiences, appeared in films, and maintained a low-profile life focused on family and equestrian pursuits until Shaw's death in 2013.
